newsitem.title: USA: U.S. envoy optimistic about Yeltsin's surgery.
newsitem.headline: U.S. envoy optimistic about Yeltsin's surgery.

text.p: U.S. envoy to Russia Thomas Pickering on Friday said he was "quite positive" about the outcome of President Boris Yeltsin's planned heart surgery.
Pickering told PBS-TV's "NewsHour with Jim Lehrer" that he had a long discussion with U.S. heart surgeon Michael DeBakey while he was in Moscow last month to examine Yeltsin.
"DeBakey was in touch with me by telephone when he was in Moscow and we had a good, long talk about President Yeltsin's health," Pickering said.
"President Yeltsin, as he prepares for surgery -- and I'm quite positive about the outcome of that -- is carrying a lighter load as he deals with the health problem he has to face," Pickering said.

Yeltsin is recovering from earlier heart attacks and is scheduled to have bypass surgery in two months to improve blood flow to his heart. DeBakey, one of the world's foremost heart surgeons and the man who pioneered the bypass procedure, said after examining Yeltsin that he expected full recovery from the operation.
Pickering said DeBakey said Yeltsin needed time to rest and get ready for the operation, but was "very positive about President Yeltsin's recovery."
Pickering praised DeBakey's expertise and his eminence in the field, saying, "the fact that the Russians are speaking with him is very, very significant."

Pickering, noting Yeltsin would transfer authority for the nuclear button to Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin while he was under anaesthesia, said the Russian leader was expected to resume his full schedule at the end of 1996 or the start of 1997.

"The government hasn't taken new initiatives and that may be something of a drawback in the current time period, but the hope and expectation is that President Yeltsin can be back to battery, so to speak, at the end of the year or the beginning of the new year," Pickering said.
